domain_setting: Warm everyday family life across a shared home, living room, garden, and relaxed reunion meal. Different generations and family relationships are shown through who is together and how they interact.
recurring_scale_anchors: Use varied, natural family groups with adults, children, and older relatives sharing simple everyday activities.
Use a round dining table, family sofa, garden bench, or shared picture album to establish a common home-and-reunion world.
Show relationships through paired interaction, shared features where appropriate, relative age, and a wider family group; never use labels or family-tree text.
Keep gender expression varied and avoid assigning roles, colors, or household tasks based on gender. Blended families are warm, ordinary, and welcoming.

polysemy_resolution_table.families: A group of related people across generations, not a family-owned business or animal taxon.
polysemy_resolution_table.son: A male child in relation to a parent, matching the family group; not a successor, follower, or religious title.
polysemy_resolution_table.child / children: Young family members; this card uses several children to match the plural form, not a single child or childish behavior.
polysemy_resolution_table.partner: A committed romantic life partner in the relationship group, not a work partner or dance partner.
polysemy_resolution_table.female / male: Biological sex terms in a matched animal pair, following the Japanese gloss for female and avoiding gendered human stereotypes; not grammatical gender or sports categories.
polysemy_resolution_table.girl: A female child or young person, not a romantic girlfriend.
polysemy_resolution_table.boy: A male child, not a romantic boyfriend.
polysemy_resolution_table.stepmother / stepmom / stepmum: A parent's spouse or partner who is a caring member of a blended family, not a cruel stepmother stereotype.
polysemy_resolution_table.stepbrother / stepsister: Children in a blended family who are not biological siblings, shown sharing a household comfortably; not antagonists in a fairy tale.
polysemy_resolution_table.brother-in-law / sister-in-law: A sibling's spouse or one's spouse's sibling, shown joining the extended family; not simply a sibling or spouse alone.
polysemy_resolution_table.cousin / niece / nephew: Extended-family roles shown with the child's parent and their sibling or sibling-in-law nearby, rather than a generic adult with child.

contrast_notes.parent / father / mother: Parent is gender-neutral care; father and mother show adult family relationships through distinct interactions without limiting the role to stereotyped activities.
contrast_notes.child / son / daughter / boy / girl: Child is plural in its card; son and daughter include a parent relationship; boy and girl are age-and-gender terms without a parent role required.
contrast_notes.grandparent / grandchildren / granddaugh: Use visible generation differences, an older relative, and one or more younger relatives; exact grandchild role is clear through the generations shown.
contrast_notes.sibling / brother / sister / stepbrother: Sibling is gender-neutral; brother and sister focus a boy or girl in a sibling pair; step-siblings share a blended-family setting and have distinct family members around them.
contrast_notes.twins / triplets: Two same-age children versus three same-age children, counted visually and differentiated from a general group of children.
contrast_notes.boyfriend / girlfriend / partner / spous: Boyfriend and girlfriend show young romantic partners; partner shows a committed couple working as a team; spouse uses wedding bands; husband and wife identify one member of a married couple.
contrast_notes.female / male: The female card focuses on a brown female mallard with ducklings; the male card focuses on a green-headed drake beside the same kind of family scene.
contrast_notes.baby / toddler / child / teenagers / adu: Show clear developmental stages through scale, movement, and age-appropriate objects: infant lying down, first walking steps, school-age children, adolescents, and grown adults.
